newsitem.title: FRANCE: French leftists cool to immigration reform.
newsitem.headline: French leftists cool to immigration reform.

text.p: French leftists and human rights groups criticised proposed immigration law reforms on Wednesday as double-edged, saying they both improved and worsened conditions for immigrants.

The opposition Socialist Party and the Movement against Racism (MRAP) said the reform planned by the conservative government would boost state controls on foreign residents and reduce judicial safeguards on expulsion of illegal immigrants.
The bill would make it easier for authorities to fight a judge's rejection of an order to expel an illegal immigrant.
Socialist Party spokesman Francois Hollande told reporters that some aspects of the plan would "unacceptably harden" the law.

On the other hand, Hollande welcomed plans to close legal loopholes which have deprived some immigrants of residence rights and led to protests by African immigrants that embarrassed the government this summer.
"This is an acknowledgement that the Pasqua laws were inhuman and could not be enforced," Hollande said.
Media reports said the government would soon offer a bill to solve legal headaches posed by the 1993 hardline immigration laws named after tough former interior minister Charles Pasqua.

The bill would give residence rights to illegal immigrants who have a French spouse or French children, or have been making a living in the country for at least 15 years, or would face serious danger if sent home.

CIMADE, a group looking after immigrants, voiced regret that the planned reform would not guarantee the right to family life by extending residence rights to illegal residents whose spouse is a legal resident, and to illegal residents who have children born in France.
The 1993 laws abolished a tradition that automatically gave French citizenship to children born in France.
